points.description: Overloaded functions are differentiated by their function signature (i.e., the number and/or types of parameters).
points.partial_credit: Half marks if only vaguely says 'by their parameters' or 'by arguments' without naming signature, or gives only one aspect with a minor error.

points.description: On a call, the compiler picks the function whose signature is closest to / best matches the call (the given arguments).
points.partial_credit: Half mark if only says it matches the call without the idea of best/closest match.

rubric.notes: Full marks for stating that overloads are told apart by their signature (parameter number/types); wording may differ. The second mark is for the compiler choosing the best-matching signature at the call. Answers that only mention return type, function name, or unrelated ideas get no marks for P1; a wrong statement loses only that point.
